_default: I look for somewhere to put it on the CRT. The CRT has no idea what that is.
I hold it up to the CRT. The screen hums. It's humming at me, not with me.
That doesn't go in a computer from 1997. Almost nothing does.
keycard: No card reader on a computer this old. It predates cards. It barely postdates fire.
code_note: I type 7314 into the CRT. Nothing. That's the front door's code, genius.
terminal_key: I press the terminal key to the CRT. Wrong terminal. This one wants a different kind of persuasion.
golden_token: There's no coin slot on the CRT. I checked twice. I really wanted there to be one.
energy_drink: Caffeine isn't electricity. The CRT doesn't need a mood boost. It needs a socket.
glasses_3d: I look at the CRT through the 3D glasses. It's still dark. In two colours.
scrap_paper: I hold the blank scrap to the screen. Nothing to print on it. The CRT has its own printer. Snob.

then.text: The CRT shows the patient roster. 'PATIENT ZERO — STATUS: ESCAPED' blinks in red at the bottom.

else.text: A green phosphor glow: 'VAULT OPEN. INSERT BACKUP.' The disk drive blinks, waiting for something to read.
An ancient CRT with a green phosphor glow. A blinking cursor: 'INSERT ADRIAN'S LEDGER. ENTER PIN.'
An ancient CRT monitor. Dark. Its plug dangles a metre short of the socket. Classic last-mile problem.

then.text: The computer shows the patient roster. 'PATIENT ZERO — STATUS: ESCAPED' blinks in red at the bottom.
I insert the floppy disk... *KRRRTTT*... The drive spins up. Data flooding the screen.
A patient roster. Chronic Airdrop Dependency... Acute Rug Pull Trauma... Terminal FOMO...
At the bottom, in red: PATIENT ZERO — STATUS: ESCAPED
The printer spits out a map. A map with no X. Very zen. Very useless.
The drive spits the floppy back out. 'BACKUP COMPLETE.' Into the pocket it goes.

else.text: The screen says 'INSERT BACKUP'. I need a disk. Somebody down here was working late.
The screen says 'INSERT ADRIAN'S LEDGER'. I need to find it somewhere.
The CRT stays dark. The plug doesn't reach the socket. I need a metre of something.

TALK.text: The CRT buzzes. It sounds like a fridge with opinions.

PICK.text: Bolted to the desk. And it weighs more than my car. Probably worth less, too.

OPEN.text: I open the disk drive. Empty. It looks hungry. For floppies, specifically.

CLOSE.text: I close the drive. The CRT keeps glowing green. Smug about it.

PUSH.text: I press a key. The screen flickers: 'DO NOT MASH KEYS.' I wasn't mashing. I was pressing. Firmly.

PULL.text: I pull the keyboard closer. A cockroach scurries out. It was here first. It has seniority.

GIVE.text: The CRT doesn't take gifts. It takes Adrian's Ledger and floppy disks. Picky eater.

LOOK.text: Wooden stairs back up. Every step creaks a different note. Adrian's basement has a xylophone.

TALK.text: The stairs creak. I translate: 'Careful. We're older than you.'

PICK.text: A loose nail sticks out of a step. I'm up to date on my tetanus. I'd like to stay that way.

CLOSE.text: Stairs don't close. Lucky. I'd be stuck down here.

PUSH.text: I push the banister. It wobbles. Held together by hope and one heroic screw.

PULL.text: I pull a loose board. Splinter. Adrian's woodwork bites. The fence warned me.

GIVE.text: I offer the stairs my respect. They creak. Accepted, I think.

LOOK.text: A small desk, a tiny monitor, papers everywhere. Somebody was working late. Or living here.

USE.text: I sit and read the papers. Sums, crossed-out sums, and 'WAGMI' circled until the pen went through.

TALK.text: I talk to the desk lamp. It flickers. A good listener. Bad at advice.

then.text: Nothing left but receipts. I don't do receipts. I'm a detective, not an accountant.

else.text: Under the papers, one blank scrap. Blank paper. In this economy. I'll take it.
I find a floppy disk hidden under the papers! The label reads: 'BACKUP - DO NOT LOSE'
And a blank scrap of paper. Blank paper. In this economy. I'll take it.

then.text: Nothing left but receipts. I don't do receipts. I'm a detective, not an accountant.

else.text: Under the papers, one blank scrap. Blank paper. In this economy. I'll take it.
I open the desk drawer. Under old receipts and dust... a 3.5 inch floppy labeled 'BACKUP - DO NOT LOSE'.
And a blank scrap of paper. Blank paper. In this economy. I'll take it.

CLOSE.text: I close the drawer. The dust settles back in, relieved.

PUSH.text: I push the desk. Papers go everywhere. I pick none of them up. Like a professional.

PULL.text: I pull the drawer all the way out. A dead spider and a rubber band. The spider had a good run.

GIVE.text: The desk doesn't want anything. It has enough on its plate. There's an actual plate.

LOOK.text: A bare bulb on a wire, swinging. Shadows everywhere. Finally, a room that suits a detective.

USE.text: I pull the chain. The light flickers and refuses to go out. Stubborn. I like it.

TALK.text: I stare into the light. Now I see a purple bulb everywhere. Good job, me.

PICK.text: I'm not grabbing a hot bulb. I've made bad decisions. Not hot-bulb bad.

OPEN.text: I could open a light bulb. Once. Then it's glass on the floor.

CLOSE.text: I pull the chain. Dark. Pull. Light. Dark. Light. I should probably be investigating.

PUSH.text: I push the bulb. It swings. The shadows swing. I get a little seasick.

PULL.text: I pull the wire. The bulb drops an inch. Now it's low-hanging. Like my standards.

GIVE.text: The bulb wants electricity. I've only got charm. Not compatible.

LOOK.text: Speakers, an old amp and a rack of gear. Adrian's garage-band era. Or his server era. Hard to tell.

USE.text: I flip the amp on. A low hum fills the basement. The bulb sways along.

TALK.text: I tap the microphone. 'Is this thing on?' It is. The basement now knows.

PICK.text: It's all wired together. Unplugging one thing means unplugging everything. Including me.

OPEN.text: I open the cabinet. Cables, adapters and an AUX cable. Every party's missing piece.

CLOSE.text: I close the cabinet. The cables push it open again. They want out.

else.text: The rack slides aside with a groan. Behind it — a hidden door. Still warm from the servers.
Someone didn't want this room found.

PULL.text: I pull an AUX cable. The whole rack shifts. Something behind it wants attention.

GIVE.text: The amp doesn't want gifts. It wants a guitar solo. I can't play.

LOOK.text: A worn leather armchair. It has a me-shaped dent. I've never sat in it. Probably.

USE.text: I sit. The cushion sighs. So do I. We understand each other.

TALK.text: 'What have you heard down here?' The chair creaks. Everyone's a cryptic witness tonight.

else.text: Wait... something just appeared in my pocket. A sticker? It shows a three-headed monkey. 'LOOK BEHIND YOU!' it says. Where did this come from?!

PICK.text: I check between the cushions. A quarter. A real one. I keep it. Finders keepers.

OPEN.text: I flip the cushion. Crumbs. Pizza crumbs. Upstairs pizza, I'd bet.

CLOSE.text: I put the cushion back. Nobody will ever know I was here.

PUSH.text: I push the armchair. Years of dust bunnies. A whole colony. I leave them their kingdom.

PULL.text: I pull the armrest. It comes off. I put it back. Nobody saw that.

GIVE.text: The armchair has received enough. Mostly butts and bad news.

LOOK.text: Checkered tiles, some cracked. Someone dropped something heavy down here. More than once.

USE.text: I stomp on a loose tile. It wobbles. No secret. Just bad grouting.

TALK.text: 'Hello?' My voice bounces off the tiles. The floor isn't chatty.

PICK.text: I pry up a tile. Dirt. Just dirt. I put it back like I meant to.

OPEN.text: No trapdoors. This is the bottom. Literally, for once.

CLOSE.text: The floor's closed. Any more closed and it'd be a wall.

PUSH.text: I push a tile with my foot. It clicks. My heart skips. Nothing. Thanks, tile.

PULL.text: I pull up a tile. Dirt, a worm and a bottle cap. The worm looks annoyed.

GIVE.text: The floor already has everything. Dust, footprints, a worm. It's set.

then.text: Just the cable now, dangling. The mouse lives in my pocket. It's an upgrade.

else.text: A computer mouse hanging off the desk by a frayed cable. It's given up. I recognise the look.

USE.text: I click it. The left button just sighs. This mouse has retired.

TALK.text: 'Click?' Nothing. 'Double-click?' Silence. This mouse has clicked its last.

then.text: Just a dangling cable left. The mouse has moved on to a better inventory.

else.text: I grab the mouse. The cable snaps. Well, it was already broken. Now it's portable-broken.

OPEN.text: I pop the shell open. A dusty scroll wheel and one crumb. The crumb was living there.

CLOSE.text: I snap the shell back. It won't click shut. A mouse that can't click. Poor thing.

PUSH.text: I push the mouse across the desk. It slides like it's trying to escape.

PULL.text: I pull the cable. The mouse swings like a tiny sad pendulum.

GIVE.text: Nobody here wants a dead mouse. Not even the cockroach.

LOOK.text: Notes pinned to the wall. Diagrams, arrows, and one in red marker: 'TRUST NO ONE.' Not even DOORIS?

USE.text: I try to follow the diagrams. Arrows to arrows to a drawing of a duck. Gerald gets everywhere.

TALK.text: The notes rustle in the draft. It sounds like gossip. Penny would love it down here.

PICK.text: I pull one off the wall. It reads: 'If you're reading this, check block 4,206,969.' I put it back.

OPEN.text: I unfold a note. A shopping list: ramen, BULL RUN, more ramen, 'duck food?'

CLOSE.text: I fold the note back up. Some lists are private.

PUSH.text: I push the thumbtack deeper. Ow. That was my thumb. Hence the name.

PULL.text: I pull a note off. Underneath is another note that says 'STOP PULLING NOTES OFF THE WALL.'

GIVE.text: I'm not adding to the wall. It's Adrian's conspiracy. He can hang his own.

LOOK.text: Rusty pipes. They drip in a rhythm. Drip. Drip. Buy. ...Dex, they're pipes.

USE.text: I tap a pipe. It clangs all through the house. Somewhere upstairs, a moth panics.

TALK.text: The pipes gurgle. In plumber, that's 'call someone who isn't you.'

PICK.text: I'm not ripping pipes out of the ceiling. I've seen what happens. It's called 'a flood'.

OPEN.text: I twist a valve. Water spurts out, then stops. The pipe wheezes. That was close.

CLOSE.text: I tighten the valve. The dripping stops. Then starts again, out of spite.

PUSH.text: I push a pipe. It bows. These pipes have load-bearing anxiety. Relatable.

PULL.text: I pull a loose fitting. Rust rains on my head. I've earned that.

GIVE.text: The pipes want a plumber. They got a detective. Nobody's happy.

LOOK.text: Rough stone walls. Old and cold. This basement is older than Adrian's whole company.

USE.text: I run my hand along the stone. Cold, damp. I wipe my hand on my jeans. Detective work.

TALK.text: I talk to the wall. It lets me finish. That's more than Penny does.

PICK.text: I pry at a loose stone. It doesn't budge. It's the least loose loose stone I've met.

OPEN.text: No hidden passage. Not in this wall. ...The rack, though. That rack looks shifty.

CLOSE.text: The walls are already closed. That's their entire job.

PUSH.text: I push the wall. The wall wins. Walls always win.

PULL.text: I pull at a stone. My fingernails file a complaint.

GIVE.text: I try to bribe the wall. Incorruptible. Also a wall.

lines: Beneath the lab, forgotten machines still process blocks.
A CRT monitor flickers with data from another era.
The patient roster... the escape... Patient Zero.
The answers are down here. Buried in code.

prompt.speaker: Ledger
prompt.text: ENTER PIN. Hint: my best friend's birthday. DDMM.

zeros.text: 0000. Nobody's that lazy. Except me. Apparently.

nobday.text: Adrian's best friend? I don't even know who that is. Somebody's mail would know.

gerald.text: 0301. Gerald was born on the genesis block. Of course he was.

ok_dex.text: A vault dashboard. Portfolio, NFTs, and one line blinking: 'INSERT BACKUP'.

then.text: The CRT is already plugged in. One cord per computer. I'm not a monster.

else.text: I run the orange cord from the socket to the CRT. Exactly a metre. Last mile solved.
Click. Hum. A green glow. It's alive. It smells like 1997.
The screen blinks: 'INSERT ADRIAN'S LEDGER. ENTER PIN.'

then.text: The chip is already installed. Slot B7 is happy. Nobody else noticed.

else.text: The burned chip from AdrianAuctions... it fits the empty socket in slot B7 perfectly.
*click* A tiny 'B7 OK' appears in the corner. Nothing else changes. Some fixes are just for peace of mind.
The CRT is dead. I need to power it up first before installing any chips.

then.text: The computer already recognized Adrian's Ledger. The vault dashboard is still open.

else.text: The CRT is dead. Power first, wallet second.

then.text: Already read. The roster is printed. The disk stays with me. It said DO NOT LOSE.

else.text: I insert the floppy disk... *KRRRTTT*... The drive spins up. Data flooding the screen.
A patient roster. Chronic Airdrop Dependency... Acute Rug Pull Trauma... Terminal FOMO...
At the bottom, in red: PATIENT ZERO — STATUS: ESCAPED
The printer spits out a map. A map with no X. Very zen. Very useless.
The drive spits the floppy back out. 'BACKUP COMPLETE.' Into the pocket it goes.

then.text: 'ACCESS DENIED. LEDGER REQUIRED.' The vault first, then the backup.

else.text: The CRT is dead. A floppy won't fix that. Nothing from the nineties ever fixed anything.

then.text: The CRT still displays Adrian's hidden message. The cursor blinks patiently, like it has all the time in the world. Because it does. It's a computer.

else.text: I slide a floppy from the box into the drive. The CRT goes dark. Then...
*KRRRRTTTT-KRRRRTTTT* The drive spins up like it's been WAITING for this exact disc. The screen floods with green text.
'ADRIANLAB FLOPPY COLLECTION DETECTED — HOLDER OVERRIDE ACTIVE. Decrypting Sector Zero...'
A hidden partition opens. Adrian left a personal message encoded in the floppy metadata:
'To whoever holds these discs: you're not just a collector. You backed the lab when nobody believed pixel art on a blockchain was worth anything. You were right. — A.'
Below the message, a manifest: every floppy disc ever minted, every pack opened, every trait unlocked. The entire AdrianLAB creation history. On a 1.44MB floppy. Somehow.
The CRT prints a final line: 'COMPRESSION RATIO: infinity. When you believe in the art, size doesn't matter.'
SECTOR ZERO — Unlocked Adrian's hidden floppy message
